questions.question: Which of the following is a core value expressed in the Agile Manifesto?
options: Comprehensive documentation over working software
Individuals and interactions over processes and tools
Contract negotiation over customer collaboration
Following a plan over responding to change
questions.explanation: The Agile Manifesto values individuals and interactions over processes and tools, among its four core value statements.

questions.question: The 'whole team approach' in agile testing means that:
options: Only dedicated testers are responsible for quality
Quality is a shared responsibility across developers, testers, and other roles on the team
Testing occurs only after the whole project is complete
Product owners are solely responsible for writing test cases
questions.explanation: The whole-team approach means quality and testing responsibility is shared among all team members, not isolated to a single tester role.

questions.question: Which of the following is a common characteristic shared by most agile methods (e.g. Scrum, XP, Kanban)?
options: A single, multi-year release plan with no intermediate deliverables
Iterative and incremental delivery of working software in short cycles, with frequent feedback
A strict prohibition on any face-to-face communication
Complete documentation of all requirements before any coding begins
questions.explanation: Agile methods generally favor iterative, incremental development with short cycles and frequent feedback over big-bang, fully-documented-upfront approaches.

questions.question: In Scrum, what is the PRIMARY purpose of a sprint retrospective?
options: To demonstrate completed work to stakeholders
To reflect on the past sprint and identify process improvements for future sprints
To estimate the size of upcoming backlog items
To assign new user stories to the sprint backlog
questions.explanation: The sprint retrospective is a Scrum event where the team reflects on how the sprint went (people, process, tools) and identifies improvements to carry into future sprints.

questions.question: Which Scrum artifact represents the ordered list of everything that might be needed in the product?
options: The sprint backlog
The product backlog
The burndown chart
The definition of done
questions.explanation: The product backlog is the single, ordered list of features, requirements, and fixes that could be needed in the product, managed by the product owner.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a 'definition of done' in an agile team?
options: To describe the long-term product vision
To provide a shared, agreed checklist of criteria that a user story or increment must satisfy to be considered complete
To list only the defects found in the current sprint
To replace the need for any acceptance criteria on user stories
questions.explanation: The definition of done is a shared understanding, agreed by the team, of the criteria (e.g. tested, documented, reviewed) that must be met for work to be considered complete.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST distinguishes 'acceptance criteria' from 'definition of done'?
options: Acceptance criteria are specific conditions a single user story must satisfy; definition of done is a generic checklist applying to all stories
They are exactly the same concept and used interchangeably in all agile teams
Definition of done only applies to non-functional requirements
Acceptance criteria apply project-wide, while definition of done applies to a single story only
questions.explanation: Acceptance criteria describe conditions specific to an individual story, while definition of done is a broader, team-wide checklist applicable across all stories.

questions.question: Which practice BEST supports 'continuous testing' within an agile team?
options: Delaying all testing until the very last day of the sprint
Integrating test activities throughout the sprint, alongside development, with automated regression suites run frequently
Testing only once per quarter, regardless of sprint cadence
Only performing manual exploratory testing after release
questions.explanation: Continuous testing means test activities happen throughout development (not just at the end), supported by frequent automated regression execution to give fast feedback.

questions.question: The 'Agile Testing Quadrants' model classifies tests along which two dimensions?
options: Manual vs. automated, and cost vs. benefit
Business-facing vs. technology-facing, and tests that support the team vs. tests that critique the product
Fast vs. slow, and cheap vs. expensive
Functional vs. security only
questions.explanation: The Agile Testing Quadrants classify tests by whether they are business-facing or technology-facing, and whether they support the team (guide development) or critique the product (evaluate the finished product).

questions.question: Which quadrant of the Agile Testing Quadrants would automated unit tests and component tests typically fall into?
options: Q1: Technology-facing tests that support the team
Q2: Business-facing tests that support the team
Q3: Business-facing tests that critique the product
Q4: Technology-facing tests that critique the product
questions.explanation: Unit and component tests are technology-facing (focused on internal code correctness) and support the team by giving developers fast feedback during development.

questions.question: In agile teams, why might exploratory testing be particularly valuable near the end of a sprint?
options: Because scripted tests are no longer allowed once a story is coded
Because it can uncover issues that scripted tests, written from the same assumptions as the story, might miss
Because exploratory testing always takes less time than any scripted test
Because it removes the need for a definition of done
questions.explanation: Exploratory testing brings a fresh, investigative perspective that can reveal issues scripted tests (derived from the same acceptance criteria) may not cover.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST describes the tester's role on a cross-functional agile team?
options: Testers work in isolation and only interact with the team at the very end of the project
Testers collaborate closely with developers and the product owner throughout the sprint, contributing to story refinement, test design, and quality feedback
Testers are solely responsible for writing all production code
Testers never participate in sprint planning or backlog refinement
questions.explanation: On agile teams, testers are embedded and collaborate continuously with developers and the product owner — from story refinement through test design and execution — rather than working in a separate, siloed phase.

questions.question: Which of the following skills is especially valuable for a tester participating in backlog refinement sessions?
options: The ability to ask clarifying questions that reveal missing or ambiguous acceptance criteria before development starts
The ability to write only automated performance test scripts
The ability to approve the sprint budget
The ability to assign story points without consulting the team
questions.explanation: A key value testers bring to refinement is asking probing questions about edge cases, ambiguity, and missing acceptance criteria, helping the team define clearer, more testable stories.

questions.question: Which soft skill is generally considered ESSENTIAL for testers working in agile teams, given the emphasis on collaboration?
options: Strong written and verbal communication to collaborate effectively with developers, product owners, and other stakeholders
Avoiding all communication with developers to remain independent
Working exclusively at night to avoid interacting with the team
Refusing to give feedback during stand-ups
questions.explanation: Because agile testers work closely and continuously with the whole team, strong communication and collaboration skills are essential to their effectiveness.

questions.chapter: 4. Agile Testing Methods, Techniques, and Tools
questions.question: Which test technique is commonly used in agile teams to derive test cases and drive development directly from concrete examples of desired behavior?
options: Behavior-driven development (BDD) using Given-When-Then scenarios
Waterfall-style big design up front
Static analysis of legacy code only
Manual code reviews with no test cases at all
questions.explanation: BDD uses concrete, example-based scenarios (often in Given-When-Then format) that are understandable by business and technical stakeholders alike, and that can drive both development and automated testing.

questions.chapter: 4. Agile Testing Methods, Techniques, and Tools
questions.question: Test-driven development (TDD) is characterized by:
options: Writing a failing automated test first, then writing just enough production code to make it pass, then refactoring
Writing all production code first, then writing tests only after the release
Never writing any automated tests at the unit level
Testing being performed exclusively by a separate QA team, not developers
questions.explanation: TDD follows a red-green-refactor cycle: write a failing test, write minimal code to pass it, then refactor, with tests driving the design of the code.

questions.chapter: 4. Agile Testing Methods, Techniques, and Tools
questions.question: Which of the following is a key reason agile teams invest heavily in test automation at the unit and API level?
options: To provide fast, reliable feedback on regressions within short iterations, supporting frequent integration and delivery
Because manual testing is prohibited by the Agile Manifesto
Because unit and API tests are the only tests agile teams are allowed to write
To eliminate the need for any exploratory testing
questions.explanation: Fast, reliable automated tests at the unit/API level give quick regression feedback that fits within the short iteration cycles typical of agile development.

questions.chapter: 4. Agile Testing Methods, Techniques, and Tools
questions.question: Which of the following is a common CHALLENGE when maintaining a large suite of agile automated regression tests over time?
options: Automated tests never need to change once written
As the application evolves, tests can become brittle or outdated, requiring ongoing maintenance to stay valuable and avoid false failures
Automated tests always run instantly regardless of suite size
Test automation removes the pesticide paradox entirely
questions.explanation: As the application changes, automated tests can become outdated or brittle, generating false failures or missing new risk areas unless actively maintained and reviewed.

questions.question: Which of the following is a value expressed in the Agile Manifesto regarding customer relationships?
options: Customer collaboration over contract negotiation
Contract negotiation over customer collaboration
Comprehensive documentation over working software
Following a plan over responding to change
questions.explanation: The Agile Manifesto values customer collaboration over strict contract negotiation, favoring ongoing engagement with customers throughout development.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST describes 'testing quadrant Q4' (technology-facing tests that critique the product)?
options: Unit tests written by developers before any code exists
Non-functional tests such as performance, load, and security testing that evaluate the finished product's technical qualities
User acceptance tests performed by business stakeholders
Story-writing workshops with the product owner
questions.explanation: Quadrant 4 covers technology-facing tests that critique the product, such as performance, load, security, and other non-functional testing typically requiring specialized tools.

questions.question: Which statement BEST describes the 'whole-team approach' in agile projects?
options: Only testers are responsible for quality throughout the project
Business representatives, developers, and testers share responsibility for quality with no defined roles
Testers work alongside developers and business representatives as part of one team, sharing responsibility for quality
Quality is solely the responsibility of a separate QA department outside the team
questions.explanation: The whole-team approach means testers, developers, and business representatives work together as a single team, collaboratively sharing responsibility for quality rather than assigning it to one isolated role.

questions.question: Which of the following is a typical output of a Scrum sprint planning meeting?
options: A finalized annual product roadmap for the next 12 months
A sprint goal and a sprint backlog of items the team commits to delivering in the sprint
A signed contract with an external vendor
A performance review for each team member
questions.explanation: Sprint planning produces a sprint goal describing the objective of the sprint, along with a sprint backlog listing the specific items the team plans to deliver during that sprint.

questions.question: Which of the following is a key principle behind the Agile Manifesto regarding working software?
options: Comprehensive documentation is the primary measure of progress
Working software is delivered frequently, with a preference for shorter timescales
Working software should only be delivered at the end of the project
Working software is less important than following a detailed plan
questions.explanation: One of the twelve Agile Manifesto principles states that working software should be delivered frequently, from a couple of weeks to a couple of months, with a preference for shorter timescales.

questions.question: In Kanban, what is the purpose of setting Work In Progress (WIP) limits?
options: To restrict the number of team members allowed on a project
To limit the number of items in a given workflow stage at one time, helping identify bottlenecks and improve flow
To limit the number of story points a team can estimate per sprint
To cap the total number of defects that can be logged
questions.explanation: WIP limits restrict how many work items may be in a particular stage of the workflow simultaneously, which surfaces bottlenecks and encourages a smoother, more predictable flow of work.

questions.question: Which lifecycle characteristic distinguishes Extreme Programming (XP) from many other agile approaches?
options: It forbids any form of automated testing
It strongly emphasizes technical practices such as test-driven development, pair programming, and continuous integration
It mandates a fixed one-year release cycle
It requires a dedicated, separate testing phase after coding is complete
questions.explanation: XP places heavy emphasis on technical engineering practices, including test-driven development, pair programming, refactoring, and continuous integration, to support high-quality, frequently released software.

questions.question: How does the role of testing typically differ between agile and traditional sequential development?
options: In agile, testing is a discrete phase that occurs only after all coding is finished
In agile, testing activities are integrated throughout each iteration alongside development
In agile, testing is eliminated entirely in favor of manual acceptance by the customer
In agile, only regression testing is performed, and no new tests are created
questions.explanation: Agile approaches integrate testing continuously within each iteration rather than treating it as a separate, later phase, enabling fast feedback on quality throughout development.

questions.question: What is a 'definition of done' used for in agile projects?
options: It specifies the marketing plan for a released feature
It provides a shared checklist of criteria a work item must satisfy to be considered complete
It sets the hourly rate for contracted testers
It replaces the need for any acceptance criteria on user stories
questions.explanation: A definition of done is an agreed checklist of criteria (e.g., coded, tested, reviewed, documented) that a backlog item must meet before it can be considered complete.

questions.question: Why is regression testing particularly important in agile iterations?
options: Because agile projects never modify existing code
Because frequent changes and integrations across short iterations increase the risk of unintended side effects on existing functionality
Because regression testing replaces the need for unit testing
Because it is required only during the final release sprint
questions.explanation: Since agile iterations involve frequent code changes and integrations, regression testing is critical to catch unintended side effects on previously working functionality as early as possible.

questions.question: In the agile testing quadrants model, where would automated unit tests that support the team (technology-facing) typically be placed?
options: Quadrant 1: technology-facing tests that support the team
Quadrant 2: business-facing tests that support the team
Quadrant 3: business-facing tests that critique the product
Quadrant 4: technology-facing tests that critique the product
questions.explanation: Quadrant 1 covers technology-facing tests that support the team, such as unit and component tests, usually automated and run frequently during development.

questions.question: Which agile testing quadrant contains business-facing tests that critique the product, such as exploratory testing and usability testing?
options: Quadrant 1
Quadrant 2
Quadrant 3
Quadrant 4
questions.explanation: Quadrant 3 contains business-facing tests that critique the product, including exploratory testing, usability testing, and user acceptance testing, typically performed manually.

questions.question: Which skill is especially valuable for a tester working within an agile team?
options: The ability to work in isolation without communicating with developers
Strong collaboration and communication skills to work closely with developers and business representatives
Exclusive expertise in only one testing tool
Avoidance of any involvement in requirements discussions
questions.explanation: Agile testers need strong interpersonal and communication skills because they collaborate closely and continuously with developers, product owners, and other stakeholders.

questions.question: What does it mean for an agile tester to have a 'generalizing specialist' skill set?
options: The tester only performs test execution and nothing else
The tester has deep expertise in testing while also being able to contribute to other project activities, such as requirements or automation
The tester avoids learning any new tools or techniques
The tester specializes exclusively in a single technology stack for their entire career
questions.explanation: A generalizing specialist has a core area of expertise (such as testing) but is also able to contribute in other areas, increasing flexibility for the whole team.

questions.question: What value does an agile tester typically add during backlog refinement sessions?
options: Estimating the exact hours developers will spend coding
Asking clarifying questions and identifying missing acceptance criteria or edge cases in user stories
Deciding the final release date for the product
Writing the production code for the story being refined
questions.explanation: During backlog refinement, testers contribute a quality perspective by asking questions that uncover ambiguity, missing acceptance criteria, and edge cases before development begins.

questions.question: Why is it important for agile testers to understand the business domain of the product they are testing?
options: So they can better identify realistic test scenarios and prioritize testing based on business risk and value
Domain knowledge is not relevant to agile testers
Because it eliminates the need for the product owner to write acceptance criteria
So they can write the technical architecture documentation instead of developers
questions.explanation: Understanding the business domain helps testers design realistic scenarios and prioritize their efforts based on what matters most to end users and stakeholders.

questions.chapter: 4. Agile Testing Methods, Techniques, and Tools
questions.question: What is the main purpose of Acceptance Test-Driven Development (ATDD)?
options: To write acceptance tests only after the feature has been fully coded and deployed
To collaboratively define acceptance criteria and tests, expressed in business terms, before development of a feature begins
To automate only performance and load testing scenarios
To replace unit testing entirely with manual acceptance testing
questions.explanation: ATDD involves the whole team collaborating to define acceptance tests, written in business-readable terms, before coding starts, guiding development toward satisfying those criteria.

questions.chapter: 4. Agile Testing Methods, Techniques, and Tools
questions.question: In Behavior-Driven Development (BDD), what is a common format used to express scenarios?
options: UML sequence diagrams
Given/When/Then structured natural-language statements
SQL queries against the test database
Binary decision tables only
questions.explanation: BDD commonly expresses scenarios using the Given/When/Then format, which describes preconditions, an action or event, and the expected outcome in a way that is readable by both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

questions.chapter: 4. Agile Testing Methods, Techniques, and Tools
questions.question: Which practice involves writing a failing automated test before writing the minimal production code to make it pass?
options: Exploratory testing
Test-Driven Development (TDD)
Static analysis
Risk-based test prioritization
questions.explanation: Test-Driven Development (TDD) follows a red-green-refactor cycle: write a failing test first, write minimal code to pass it, then refactor while keeping tests green.

questions.chapter: 4. Agile Testing Methods, Techniques, and Tools
questions.question: Which of the following BEST describes exploratory testing in the context of an agile iteration?
options: A fully scripted process with no room for tester judgment
Simultaneous test design, execution, and learning, guided by the tester's experience and used to complement scripted tests
A technique used only for load and performance testing
A documentation review activity performed before coding starts
questions.explanation: Exploratory testing combines test design and execution simultaneously, relying on tester skill and creativity to investigate the product, and is often used to complement predefined scripted tests in agile iterations.

questions.chapter: 4. Agile Testing Methods, Techniques, and Tools
questions.question: What is the primary benefit of maintaining a continuous integration (CI) pipeline that runs automated tests on every commit?
options: It removes the need for any manual testing on the project
It provides fast feedback on whether new changes have broken existing functionality
It guarantees that the software has zero defects before release
It replaces the need for a version control system
questions.explanation: Running automated tests on every commit via CI provides rapid feedback to the team about whether recent changes have introduced regressions, supporting agile's emphasis on fast feedback loops.

questions.chapter: 4. Agile Testing Methods, Techniques, and Tools
questions.question: When selecting tools to support agile testing, which factor should be given the HIGHEST priority?
options: The tool's popularity on social media
Whether the tool fits the team's technical context, workflow, and integrates well with the existing toolchain
Choosing the most expensive tool available on the market
Selecting a tool used by a competitor, regardless of fit
questions.explanation: Tool selection in agile testing should be driven by fit with the team's context, existing toolchain, and workflow needs, rather than cost, popularity, or imitation of competitors.

questions.question: A new legal rule is announced halfway through a sprint and affects the feature currently being built. What is the MOST agile response?
options: Continue as originally planned and discuss the law after the sprint
Collaborate immediately with the product owner and team to understand impact and adapt the sprint plan as needed
Freeze all development until a new annual project plan is approved
Ask testers to document the risk but avoid changing scope
questions.explanation: Agile teams respond to significant change quickly through collaboration. They adapt plans based on new information instead of blindly following an outdated plan.

questions.question: What is a strong example of testing starting early on an agile story?
options: Writing acceptance examples while the story is still being discussed
Waiting until coding is finished before thinking about tests
Running a full regression suite only after deployment
Logging defects from last sprint without reviewing the new story
questions.explanation: Agile testing starts as soon as a story is being shaped. Early examples improve understanding before code exists.

questions.question: What is a useful tester contribution during sprint planning?
options: Ensuring testing tasks, environments, and dependencies are considered when selecting stories
Approving payroll for the sprint team
Assigning each story to a single specialist before discussion
Avoiding all estimates so planning stays short
questions.explanation: Testers help the team make realistic commitments by surfacing quality work and dependencies early. That improves planning accuracy.

questions.chapter: 4. Agile Testing Methods, Techniques, and Tools
questions.question: What is the most useful output of an ATDD-style conversation before coding starts?
options: A set of shared examples that clarify behavior and can later become executable checks
A complete defect log for the sprint
A promise that no further clarification will be needed
A technical architecture diagram approved by management
questions.explanation: ATDD aims to build shared understanding through concrete examples. Those examples often become acceptance tests later.

questions.question: Why do agile teams prefer delivering small vertical slices of functionality instead of large partially finished components?
options: Small slices reduce the need for any testing
Small slices let the team get usable feedback sooner on working software
Large components are banned by agile methods
Vertical slices remove the need for prioritization
questions.explanation: A small vertical slice delivers end-to-end value and can be evaluated by users quickly. That earlier feedback helps the team learn and adjust.

questions.question: During backlog refinement, a tester asks, 'What should happen if the discount code is expired?' What is the primary value of that question?
options: It delays planning with unnecessary detail
It helps reveal missing acceptance criteria and edge cases before implementation starts
It proves the story should be moved to the next release
It replaces the need for customer input
questions.explanation: Questions about edge cases expose hidden behavior early. That reduces rework and makes the story more testable.

questions.question: In a daily stand-up, which update from a tester is MOST valuable?
options: A detailed review of every test case executed yesterday
A short update on current progress, quality risks, and blockers affecting the sprint goal
A private complaint sent only to the Scrum Master after the meeting
A list of defects from previous releases unrelated to current work
questions.explanation: Stand-ups work best when updates are brief and relevant to team coordination. Risks and blockers help the whole team adapt.

questions.chapter: 4. Agile Testing Methods, Techniques, and Tools
questions.question: In a BDD scenario written as Given/When/Then, what does the 'Then' part describe?
options: The expected outcome after the action occurs
The deployment steps for the environment
The people assigned to automate the test
The historical reason the feature was requested
questions.explanation: In Given/When/Then, the Then section states the expected result. It captures what should be observed after the behavior is triggered.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of a daily stand-up in an agile team?
options: To approve timesheets for the previous day
To synchronize the team and plan the next day's work toward the current goal
To conduct detailed defect triage for all open issues
To replace backlog refinement meetings
questions.explanation: The daily stand-up is a short coordination event. Its purpose is to improve shared awareness and help the team organize its next steps.

questions.question: Which activity is the BEST example of a business-facing test that supports the team?
options: Discussing concrete acceptance examples before coding begins
Stress-testing the production database cluster
Reviewing CPU utilization after release
Running a vulnerability scanner against the deployed system
questions.explanation: Business-facing tests that support the team help clarify desired behavior before or during development. Acceptance examples are a typical case.

questions.question: A product owner writes acceptance criteria that say only 'works as expected.' How can a tester add the MOST value?
options: Accept the wording because details can wait for execution
Help turn the vague statement into specific examples and observable outcomes
Replace the criteria with a defect report template
Estimate the story in hours without further discussion
questions.explanation: Testers often add value by making expectations concrete and verifiable. Specific examples reduce misunderstanding later.

questions.chapter: 4. Agile Testing Methods, Techniques, and Tools
questions.question: In the TDD cycle, why is the refactor step important after the test passes?
options: It allows the team to improve code design while keeping behavior protected by tests
It is when acceptance criteria are first written
It replaces the need for code review
It should be skipped to preserve velocity
questions.explanation: Refactoring improves internal structure without changing behavior. Passing tests give confidence that design improvements did not break intent.

questions.question: How does a Definition of Ready help an agile team before work starts on a backlog item?
options: It guarantees the item will be defect-free when delivered
It provides a shared check that the item is understood well enough to begin without avoidable confusion
It replaces sprint planning entirely
It is used only by testers to reject stories
questions.explanation: A Definition of Ready helps the team notice when a story is too unclear or incomplete to start efficiently. It reduces churn caused by avoidable ambiguity.

questions.question: Within a sprint, what is usually the MOST effective way to get fast confidence on a new story?
options: Rely mainly on a single end-to-end UI test because it looks realistic
Use a mix of fast lower-level tests and a smaller number of higher-level checks
Delay all testing until several stories can be tested together
Skip lower-level testing if exploratory testing is planned
questions.explanation: A balanced mix gives fast feedback and broader coverage. Over-relying on a few slow UI tests usually reduces speed and diagnosis quality.

questions.question: Why might an agile tester collaborate with operations or platform engineers before release?
options: To define logging, monitoring, or deployment checks that support quality in production-like environments
To transfer all testing responsibility away from the team
To avoid discussing non-functional risks during the sprint
To remove the need for automated tests
questions.explanation: Quality feedback does not stop at the test environment. Collaboration with operations can improve observability and deployment confidence.

questions.chapter: 4. Agile Testing Methods, Techniques, and Tools
questions.question: What is the main goal of running a CI pipeline on every commit?
options: To delay feedback until the entire sprint is complete
To provide rapid evidence when a change breaks build or test expectations
To replace version control branching
To remove the need for local testing
questions.explanation: Frequent CI runs shorten the time between introducing a change and learning its effect. Fast feedback is central to agile delivery.

questions.question: During sprint planning, the team can either add one more customer-facing story or spend that effort paying down test automation debt that recently slowed delivery. Which choice BEST reflects agile thinking?
options: Always choose the extra story because visible scope matters more than technical work
Ignore automation debt until the release is complete
Consider the effect on sustainable delivery and product quality before deciding with the product owner
Let only the Scrum Master decide because technical debt is not a backlog concern
questions.explanation: Agile teams balance immediate feature value with technical work that preserves quality and flow. Technical debt is a product concern because it affects future speed and risk.

questions.question: The sprint is almost over and only half of the regression suite can be run. How should testing be prioritized?
options: Execute tests randomly to keep the process fair
Focus on areas with recent changes, important business flows, and known fragility
Run only tests owned by the tester who found the most defects last sprint
Skip regression entirely because agile teams accept constant change
questions.explanation: Risk-based selection is appropriate when time is limited. Recent changes and critical flows are more likely to expose important regressions.

questions.question: How does business domain knowledge help an agile tester most directly?
options: It lets the tester replace the product owner on roadmap decisions
It helps identify realistic scenarios, risks, and priorities that matter to users
It removes the need for technical skills
It guarantees that all defects can be found manually
questions.explanation: Knowing the domain helps testers focus on behavior that matters. It improves both scenario design and prioritization.

questions.chapter: 4. Agile Testing Methods, Techniques, and Tools
questions.question: When is service virtualization especially useful in agile testing?
options: When the team depends on an external system that is unavailable, costly, or hard to control during testing
When all real integrations are fast and always accessible
When the goal is to eliminate contract checking entirely
When developers want to avoid learning the real API
questions.explanation: Virtual services can remove blockers caused by unavailable or unstable dependencies. They allow earlier and more repeatable testing.

questions.question: What does a sustainable pace in agile development primarily aim to achieve?
options: Keeping the team working overtime near the end of every iteration
Maintaining a rhythm that can continue over time without burning out the team
Reducing collaboration so people can focus only on their specialty
Ensuring every story is estimated in hours
questions.explanation: A sustainable pace helps the team remain effective over the long term. Constant overtime tends to reduce quality and predictability.

questions.question: After fixing a defect in tax calculation, which regression testing choice is MOST sensible?
options: Retest only the exact screen where the defect appeared and nothing related
Retest the fix and nearby calculation paths that could be affected by the change
Avoid retesting because the developer already checked it
Wait until the next major release to run any regression
questions.explanation: A defect fix can affect related logic beyond the exact symptom. Agile regression testing should include the changed area and likely side effects.

questions.question: A developer says a story is finished, but a key acceptance example still fails. What is the MOST effective tester response?
options: Quietly mark the story done to avoid conflict
Present the failing evidence and discuss the gap against the agreed completion criteria with the team
Reassign the defect to the product owner without explanation
Wait until after release to mention the issue
questions.explanation: Agile testers communicate quality concerns with evidence tied to shared agreements. That keeps the conversation objective and collaborative.

questions.chapter: 4. Agile Testing Methods, Techniques, and Tools
questions.question: What is the main purpose of contract tests between collaborating services?
options: To measure page-load speed from the browser
To verify that each side still honors the agreed interface and data expectations
To replace all unit tests in both services
To document deployment runbooks
questions.explanation: Contract tests focus on integration expectations between systems. They give earlier warning when interface assumptions drift.

questions.question: What is a key benefit of using story mapping when planning a product?
options: It automatically assigns developers to tasks
It helps the team visualize the user journey and identify thin releases and missing slices
It replaces the need for acceptance criteria
It is mainly used to calculate infrastructure cost
questions.explanation: Story mapping shows how user activities and stories fit together. That view helps the team find gaps and plan incremental releases.

questions.question: What makes an exploratory testing charter useful during a sprint?
options: It gives a focused mission for investigation while still leaving room for tester learning and judgment
It specifies every test step so nothing unexpected can be explored
It is only needed when automated testing is impossible
It replaces all reporting after the session
questions.explanation: A charter frames what to investigate without turning the session into a rigid script. That balance supports purposeful exploration.

questions.question: A tester and developer disagree about defect severity. What is the BEST way to resolve it?
options: Escalate immediately to senior management
Discuss user impact, business risk, and evidence using shared severity guidance
Let the tester decide alone because they found it
Close the defect to keep the sprint moving
questions.explanation: Severity discussions are most productive when grounded in impact and agreed criteria. Shared evidence reduces unhelpful opinion battles.

questions.chapter: 4. Agile Testing Methods, Techniques, and Tools
questions.question: Why are test doubles such as mocks or stubs often used in lower-level automated tests?
options: They help isolate the unit under test and make checks faster and more controllable
They guarantee that production integrations never need testing
They are required for every acceptance test
They replace assertions in test code
questions.explanation: Test doubles let the team control dependencies and focus on the behavior being exercised. That usually improves test speed and diagnosis.

questions.question: An agile team adds a short research item because a new payment provider has unknown integration constraints. What is the purpose of that spike?
options: To deliver production-ready functionality to customers
To postpone estimation until after deployment
To gain knowledge that reduces uncertainty for later implementation work
To replace exploratory testing with documentation
questions.explanation: A spike is a time-boxed investigation used to learn enough to make better delivery decisions. It is about reducing uncertainty, not shipping full functionality.

questions.question: In session-based exploratory testing, what is the value of a debrief after a session?
options: It lets the tester discard all notes once time expires
It helps share findings, risks, and next ideas with the team
It is used to estimate sprint velocity
It replaces backlog refinement for the next sprint
questions.explanation: A debrief makes exploratory work visible and useful to others. It turns individual learning into shared team insight.

questions.question: Which practice is especially helpful for testers on a distributed agile team?
options: Relying mainly on hallway conversations that are not recorded
Sharing concise written evidence, examples, and session notes asynchronously
Waiting for monthly status meetings to raise quality risks
Avoiding screen sharing to protect independence
questions.explanation: Distributed teams benefit from lightweight, visible artifacts that others can review later. Good asynchronous communication reduces delays.

questions.chapter: 4. Agile Testing Methods, Techniques, and Tools
questions.question: Why do agile teams often automate many checks at the API or service level instead of only through the UI?
options: API checks are usually faster and less brittle while still validating important business behavior
UI testing is forbidden in continuous integration
API checks can verify usability better than humans
Service-level checks remove the need for any unit tests
questions.explanation: Service-level tests often balance realism and speed effectively. They usually fail more precisely and require less maintenance than heavy UI suites.

questions.question: In a Kanban system, what does a pull approach encourage?
options: Starting new work as soon as anyone is free, regardless of downstream capacity
Taking new work only when there is capacity in the next step of the workflow
Assigning all work from a central project manager
Moving items to done at the end of each month
questions.explanation: A pull system limits overloading downstream stages. Work is started when there is real capacity to handle it.

questions.question: A team adds 'search results appear within two seconds for 95% of requests' to a story. How should that statement be treated?
options: As unnecessary detail because agile stories should avoid measurable limits
As a non-functional acceptance criterion that should influence development and testing within the iteration
As a release note item only after the feature ships
As something testers can evaluate only in production
questions.explanation: Non-functional needs can be expressed as acceptance criteria when they matter to the story. Making them explicit allows the team to design and test for them early.

questions.question: How can a tester coach the team in exploratory testing without becoming a bottleneck?
options: By teaching charters and heuristics so others can investigate risks as well
By keeping exploratory ideas private until release day
By insisting only testers are allowed to explore
By replacing all scripted tests with unscripted sessions
questions.explanation: Coaching spreads testing skill across the team. That supports the whole-team approach instead of centralizing knowledge.

questions.chapter: 4. Agile Testing Methods, Techniques, and Tools
questions.question: A test fails intermittently with no product defect found. What is the best team response to that flaky test?
options: Ignore it permanently because occasional failure is normal
Treat it as a quality problem, investigate the cause, and avoid letting it pollute pipeline feedback
Count each failure as a confirmed production defect
Duplicate it ten times so at least one instance passes
questions.explanation: Flaky tests erode trust in automation. Teams should address their causes so pipeline results remain meaningful.

questions.question: On a cumulative flow diagram, the testing band keeps getting wider over several days. What does that MOST likely suggest?
options: Testing has become a bottleneck and work is accumulating there
The product owner has reordered the backlog
The team has reduced cycle time
Developers have stopped committing code
questions.explanation: A widening band shows growing work-in-progress in that stage. That usually indicates reduced flow or a bottleneck.

questions.question: Which statement about test levels in agile teams is MOST accurate?
options: Unit, integration, and system testing may overlap within the same iteration
Only system testing is performed during the sprint
Each test level must wait for formal sign-off from the previous level
User acceptance testing always starts after release
questions.explanation: Agile work is iterative, so multiple test levels often happen within the same sprint. They are not strictly separated into long phases.

questions.question: What value can a tester bring when pairing with a developer on unit-test ideas?
options: A focus on edge cases and failure modes drawn from previous defects and business rules
Approval authority over coding style
The ability to skip acceptance criteria
A guarantee that no further review is needed
questions.explanation: Testers often think in terms of boundaries, negative paths, and risks. Bringing those ideas into lower-level tests improves early defect detection.

questions.chapter: 4. Agile Testing Methods, Techniques, and Tools
questions.question: How does static analysis support agile testing?
options: It finds every runtime defect that users might ever see
It can detect certain issues early without executing the software, adding another fast feedback mechanism
It replaces all peer review and unit testing
It is useful only after a feature is released
questions.explanation: Static analysis provides quick feedback on some classes of issues before runtime. It complements, rather than replaces, dynamic testing.

questions.question: Which action best shows a Scrum Master acting as a servant leader?
options: Assigning each developer a fixed set of tasks for the sprint
Helping the team remove impediments and improve how they work
Approving every automated test before it runs
Owning the product backlog priority order
questions.explanation: A servant leader supports the team rather than directing every task. Removing impediments and enabling improvement is a core Scrum Master contribution.

questions.question: Why should test data needs be discussed while refining a story instead of during final test execution?
options: Because test data cannot be changed once a sprint starts
Because early preparation avoids delays and exposes hidden business rules
Because only developers are allowed to create test data
Because manual testing should not use data variations
questions.explanation: Thinking about data early reveals constraints and avoids late surprises. It also helps the team understand how the feature will really be verified.

questions.question: Before a sprint review, how can a tester support the team most effectively?
options: Prepare realistic scenarios or data that show whether the delivered behavior meets expectations
Rewrite the product roadmap for the next quarter
Suppress known issues so the demo looks smoother
Approve all backlog estimates personally
questions.explanation: A good review benefits from realistic examples of what was built. Testers can help the team show actual behavior clearly.

questions.chapter: 4. Agile Testing Methods, Techniques, and Tools
questions.question: Why can code coverage be misleading if used as the main indicator of test quality?
options: High coverage does not show whether the tests assert the right behavior or meaningful risks
Coverage automatically proves the absence of defects
Coverage can be collected only for UI tests
Low coverage always means the product is unsafe to release
questions.explanation: Coverage shows what code was executed, not whether the right things were verified. Useful tests require meaningful assertions and good risk focus.

questions.question: How does a sprint review differ from a sprint retrospective?
options: The review inspects the product increment with stakeholders, while the retrospective inspects the team's way of working
The review focuses on team process, while the retrospective approves scope changes
Both meetings have the same purpose but different names
The retrospective is only for managers, while the review is only for developers
questions.explanation: The sprint review centers on the product and stakeholder feedback. The retrospective focuses on improving the team's process, tools, and collaboration.

questions.question: A defect is found late in the sprint. What is the BEST first response from the agile team?
options: Wait for the retrospective before discussing it
Collaboratively assess impact and decide whether to fix now, defer, or reduce scope
Close the defect because late issues are expected in agile
Assign blame to the person who wrote the code
questions.explanation: Agile teams handle problems transparently and collaboratively. The immediate goal is to understand impact and make a practical decision together.

questions.question: Which statement BEST describes tester independence in a mature agile team?
options: Testers stay fully independent only by avoiding daily collaboration
Independence comes from bringing objective challenge and evidence, even while working closely with the team
Independence means testers own the product backlog
Independence is unnecessary if automated tests exist
questions.explanation: Agile teams value close collaboration, but they still need objective thinking. Independence is preserved through mindset, evidence, and willingness to challenge assumptions.

questions.chapter: 4. Agile Testing Methods, Techniques, and Tools
questions.question: What is the main benefit of running suitable automated tests in parallel in CI?
options: It shortens feedback time, provided tests remain isolated and repeatable
It guarantees that every failure is a product defect
It removes the need for test data management
It makes slow UI tests more precise than unit tests
questions.explanation: Parallel execution can reduce waiting time significantly. The gain depends on tests being independent and stable.

questions.question: How should a team use velocity trends during release planning?
options: As a rough forecasting aid rather than a guaranteed commitment
As a replacement for backlog prioritization
As proof that every future sprint will deliver the same number of stories
As a measure of individual tester productivity
questions.explanation: Velocity can help forecast likely capacity, but it is not a promise. Agile planning accepts uncertainty and updates forecasts with new data.

questions.question: A production defect escaped because no test covered a surprising edge case. What is the MOST useful action in the next retrospective?
options: Ban all exploratory testing
Identify why the edge case was missed and improve examples, heuristics, or automation accordingly
Remove the story from the release notes
Increase documentation volume for every future defect
questions.explanation: Retrospectives aim to improve the system of work. Understanding why a gap existed is more useful than simply adding paperwork.

questions.question: Why is it valuable for an agile tester to learn some automation skills even if developers write most framework code?
options: It allows the tester to contribute directly to faster feedback and collaborate more effectively on quality risks
It removes the need for manual or exploratory testing
It means the tester no longer needs business knowledge
It is required only so the tester can manage the CI server
questions.explanation: Automation skills increase the tester's options and improve collaboration. They help the tester contribute to repeatable checks and better feedback loops.

questions.chapter: 4. Agile Testing Methods, Techniques, and Tools
questions.question: Why might a team label a small subset of automated tests as smoke tests?
options: To identify a fast set that gives quick confidence in critical paths after a change
To mark tests that should never run in CI
To group only exploratory test session notes
To separate tests by which developer wrote them
questions.explanation: Smoke tests provide a fast first signal on whether the build is fundamentally healthy. They are not a substitute for broader regression coverage.

questions.question: Which backlog item BEST reflects the INVEST idea of being small and testable?
options: As a shopper, I can pay by credit card for all order types in every country with all tax rules implemented at once
Build the complete reporting engine
As a returning user, I can reset my password by email so I can regain access to my account
Improve quality
questions.explanation: A good INVEST story is specific enough to understand and verify while still delivering user value. The password reset story is bounded and testable.

questions.question: Which user story is the MOST testable?
options: Improve reporting
As an account holder, I can download my monthly statement as a PDF from the billing page
Make the checkout flow better
Support all future payment needs
questions.explanation: A testable story is concrete and bounded. The PDF statement story is specific enough to derive meaningful checks.

questions.question: What can a tester contribute to a retrospective besides a list of open defects?
options: Only personal complaints about other team members
Observations about escape patterns, unstable areas, and where feedback arrived too late
A final approval of next sprint scope
Daily time tracking details for each developer
questions.explanation: Useful retrospective input looks for patterns and process improvements. Testers often see where feedback quality or timing can improve.

questions.chapter: 4. Agile Testing Methods, Techniques, and Tools
questions.question: Why are short-lived, automatically created test environments useful in agile delivery?
options: They make environment setup less repeatable so teams stay flexible
They help provide consistent conditions for testing and reduce configuration drift
They remove the need for production-like data
They are mainly useful for storing manual test scripts
questions.explanation: Ephemeral environments can improve consistency and reduce 'works on my machine' problems. Automation makes them easier to provision when needed.

questions.question: A user story covers search, filtering, sorting, exporting, and saved views in one item. What is the BEST agile response?
options: Keep it intact so all related work is finished together
Split it into smaller slices that still provide user value and can be completed independently
Estimate it more precisely and start coding immediately
Move it to the Definition of Done checklist
questions.explanation: Large stories reduce feedback and increase risk. Splitting them into smaller valuable slices improves flow and makes planning and testing easier.

questions.question: How can independent testing still exist in an agile team without creating a separate late-phase test department?
options: By keeping testers uninvolved until development finishes
By having testers bring an independent critical perspective while collaborating continuously with the team
By rotating the product owner into the tester role every sprint
By forbidding developers from reviewing tests
questions.explanation: Independence in agile is often about mindset and perspective rather than organizational distance. Testers can collaborate closely and still provide objective challenge.

questions.question: Why is empathy for end users important for an agile tester?
options: It helps the tester imagine realistic workflows, frustrations, and quality expectations
It allows the tester to ignore technical constraints
It replaces the need for acceptance criteria
It matters only for customer support, not testing
questions.explanation: Empathy improves scenario design and prioritization. It helps the tester notice problems that matter to real users.

questions.chapter: 4. Agile Testing Methods, Techniques, and Tools
questions.question: How does infrastructure as code help agile testing and delivery?
options: It keeps environment definitions repeatable, reviewable, and versioned alongside changes
It guarantees perfect production performance
It replaces the need for release notes
It is relevant only to large waterfall programs
questions.explanation: Versioned environment definitions improve repeatability and collaboration. They make changes to infrastructure easier to track and review.

questions.question: From a Lean perspective, which activity is most clearly waste?
options: Waiting several days for a simple defect clarification because work is handed across departments
Pairing to solve a tricky integration problem
Refining the next few stories with the product owner
Running a fast regression suite after a code change
questions.explanation: Lean focuses on eliminating delays, handoff friction, and other non-value-adding work. Long waits for simple clarifications are classic waste.

questions.question: Which statement best contrasts confirmatory testing with exploratory testing?
options: Confirmatory testing checks expected behavior, while exploratory testing investigates beyond what was already expected
Confirmatory testing is manual only, while exploratory testing is automated only
They are the same activity with different names
Exploratory testing is done before coding, while confirmatory testing is done after release
questions.explanation: Confirmatory testing verifies expected outcomes from known requirements or examples. Exploratory testing looks for additional information, risks, and unexpected behavior.

questions.question: How can a tester support product quality after deployment in a DevOps-oriented team?
options: By helping define useful alerts, dashboards, or checks that reveal quality issues in operation
By refusing to look at production feedback because testing ends at release
By asking operations to hide incidents from the team
By removing acceptance testing from the sprint
questions.explanation: In a DevOps context, testers can help shape the feedback the team receives from real operation. Production signals are valuable learning inputs.

questions.chapter: 4. Agile Testing Methods, Techniques, and Tools
questions.question: Why should automated test scripts and related test assets be kept in version control?
options: So changes are traceable and can evolve with the product
So testers can hide failures from developers
To prevent anyone from reviewing old test logic
To avoid using CI pipelines
questions.explanation: Version control supports collaboration, traceability, and synchronized change. Test assets should evolve together with the system.

questions.question: What is a practical benefit of collective code ownership in an XP-style team?
options: Only one specialist may change each module, so accidental defects disappear
More team members can improve or fix code without waiting for a single owner
It removes the need for code review
It guarantees identical coding styles without standards
questions.explanation: Collective ownership reduces bottlenecks around a single expert. It supports faster flow when combined with good tests and shared standards.

questions.question: A sprint ends tomorrow and a high-risk payment change was merged today. Which testing approach is MOST appropriate?
options: Spend the remaining time evenly across all stories
Prioritize focused testing around the payment change and critical customer journeys it could affect
Postpone all testing because late changes are not worth examining
Run only UI smoke tests because they cover every layer
questions.explanation: Late high-risk changes deserve focused attention. Agile testing uses risk to guide where limited time will provide the most value.

questions.question: During a risk storming workshop, what is a strong tester contribution?
options: Listing only the defects found in the previous sprint
Identifying fragile flows, unlikely but costly failures, and assumptions that deserve targeted checks
Estimating velocity for the next four releases
Replacing the product owner's prioritization completely
questions.explanation: Testers are often good at spotting where failures may be subtle or expensive. That perspective strengthens risk-based planning.

questions.chapter: 4. Agile Testing Methods, Techniques, and Tools
questions.question: Why is resetting or isolating data between automated test runs important?
options: It reduces hidden coupling so results are more reliable and repeatable
It makes test execution slower without other benefits
It guarantees that UI defects disappear
It is needed only for performance tests
questions.explanation: Shared leftover data can create non-deterministic failures. Isolating or resetting state helps keep tests trustworthy.

questions.question: Why can pair programming improve quality on agile teams?
options: Because it avoids all need for automated tests
Because continuous review while coding can catch mistakes and spread knowledge early
Because it guarantees work is completed twice as fast
Because one person writes code while the other is inactive
questions.explanation: Pair programming provides immediate feedback during implementation. It can reveal defects early and share understanding across teammates.

questions.question: Why are executable acceptance tests sometimes called living documentation?
options: Because they never need updating when behavior changes
Because they describe expected system behavior in a form that can be checked repeatedly
Because only business analysts can read them
Because they are archived after each sprint and not reused
questions.explanation: When kept current, executable acceptance tests describe behavior and verify it. Their value comes from staying aligned with the software.

questions.question: The team can automate one repeated regression check this sprint or run it manually again. How can a tester add value to that discussion?
options: Argue that manual execution is always superior
Explain the trade-off between one-time automation cost and future feedback savings
Decide alone without involving the team
Postpone the decision until after release
questions.explanation: Testers can help the team balance short-term effort against recurring value. Repetition and risk often justify automation investment.

questions.chapter: 4. Agile Testing Methods, Techniques, and Tools
questions.question: What value does a visible test dashboard provide to an agile team?
options: It replaces all conversation about risk
It makes quality signals, trends, and failures easier for the team to notice and act on
It allows managers to approve every commit
It is mainly a storage place for obsolete test cases
questions.explanation: Dashboards can act as information radiators for quality. Their main value is making signals visible enough to prompt useful action.

questions.question: If an external dependency is blocking progress on a sprint item, what should the team do first?
options: Hide the issue until the sprint review
Make the impediment visible and collaborate on options to remove or work around it
Wait until the next release planning session
Close the story as done to protect the burn chart
questions.explanation: Agile teams make blockers visible quickly. Early collaboration gives the team the best chance to resolve or mitigate the problem.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of a Three Amigos discussion?
options: To approve overtime for the sprint
To build shared understanding of a backlog item from business, development, and testing perspectives
To decide annual budget targets
To replace the sprint review
questions.explanation: Three Amigos discussions align different viewpoints around a story. That shared understanding improves quality before coding begins.

questions.question: Which technical skill most helps a tester diagnose failures quickly on an agile team?
options: Reading logs, API responses, and other technical evidence to narrow possible causes
Writing only executive summaries for management
Avoiding all tool output to stay unbiased
Estimating in ideal days instead of story points
questions.explanation: Being able to inspect technical evidence improves communication with developers and speeds up problem isolation.

questions.chapter: 4. Agile Testing Methods, Techniques, and Tools
questions.question: How can accessibility-focused automation help an agile team?
options: By catching some obvious accessibility issues early so they can be addressed before later review
By proving the product is fully accessible in every real-world context
By replacing all usability testing with disabled users
By limiting testing to color contrast only
questions.explanation: Automated accessibility checks are helpful early filters. They do not prove full accessibility, but they can surface obvious issues quickly.

questions.question: Why do small batch sizes often improve flow in agile delivery?
options: They make it easier to detect problems and adjust before too much work is invested
They eliminate the need for prioritization
They guarantee that rework will never occur
They allow the team to skip backlog refinement
questions.explanation: Smaller batches shorten feedback loops and reduce the cost of discovering mistakes. That makes adaptation easier and less expensive.

questions.question: What does shifting testing left usually mean in an agile context?
options: Moving all test execution to the operations team
Bringing quality activities earlier into refinement, design, and coding
Reducing the number of testers on the team
Running only performance tests before release
questions.explanation: Shift-left means addressing quality sooner, not later. Earlier conversations and checks reduce late discovery of defects.

questions.question: How can a tester help when a story seems too large for one sprint?
options: Suggest slices and examples that break the work into smaller testable increments
Increase the estimate until it fits the sprint
Move all testing to the next sprint
Ask the Scrum Master to code part of it
questions.explanation: Testers can help find seams in behavior and data that support meaningful story splitting. Smaller slices are easier to build and verify.

questions.chapter: 4. Agile Testing Methods, Techniques, and Tools
questions.question: Why might a team include a lightweight performance benchmark in CI for a critical API?
options: To get early warning if a code change significantly degrades response behavior
To prove the system can handle any future production load
To eliminate the need for deeper non-functional testing
To measure business value directly from the pipeline
questions.explanation: A small benchmark in CI can reveal sudden regressions early. It complements, rather than replaces, deeper performance evaluation.

questions.question: A stakeholder requests a valuable change near the end of the release window. Which approach is MOST consistent with agile planning?
options: Reject the request because plans must remain fixed once the release starts
Evaluate the value and impact, then re-prioritize scope if the change is worthwhile
Add the request without discussing trade-offs with the team
Delay all current testing until the new feature is implemented
questions.explanation: Agile planning is adaptive. Teams consider the new value and trade-offs, then adjust scope deliberately rather than treating plans as immovable.

questions.question: A field accepts ages from 18 to 65 inclusive. Which set of test values BEST applies boundary value thinking?
questions.explanation: Boundary value testing focuses on values at and around the edges of the valid range. That set probes both valid and invalid boundaries.

questions.question: Why might a tester collaborate with a UX designer on a new workflow?
options: To consider usability risks and confusing interactions before customers encounter them
To replace functional testing entirely with design review
To keep developers out of user experience discussions
To avoid using acceptance criteria
questions.explanation: UX collaboration helps the team uncover usability problems early. Many quality issues are about confusing behavior, not just functional failure.

questions.chapter: 4. Agile Testing Methods, Techniques, and Tools
questions.question: When an automated UI test fails in CI, which practice most helps diagnosis?
options: Capturing useful evidence such as screenshots, logs, or network traces with the failure
Rerunning the entire pipeline without saving any artifacts
Deleting the failing test immediately
Asking the product owner to debug the test framework
questions.explanation: Good failure evidence shortens investigation time and reduces guesswork. That makes automated feedback more actionable.

questions.question: A product has a fixed regulatory release date, but not every desired feature will fit. Which strategy BEST aligns with agile delivery?
options: Fix scope and let quality vary if time becomes tight
Prioritize the most valuable and highest-risk items first so lower-value scope can be deferred if needed
Delay testing until all planned scope is coded
Require all teams to work overtime until every wish list item is included
questions.explanation: When time is fixed, agile teams manage scope actively. Delivering the most important items first preserves value and reduces risk.

questions.question: A story adds order states of New, Paid, Shipped, and Cancelled. Which test idea best uses state-transition thinking?
options: Check only that each state label is visible on screen
Verify allowed moves such as Paid to Shipped and reject invalid ones such as Cancelled to Paid
Run a performance test with 1,000 orders
Ask the product owner to re-estimate the story
questions.explanation: State-transition testing looks at valid and invalid moves between states. It is useful when workflow rules matter.

questions.question: What is the tester's best role in an example-mapping or specification workshop?
options: Act mainly as a silent observer
Contribute questions, edge cases, and test ideas that make expectations more precise
Approve architecture decisions for the whole team
Convert every example directly into a defect
questions.explanation: Testers bring a questioning mindset that sharpens shared examples. That improves clarity before development begins.

questions.chapter: 4. Agile Testing Methods, Techniques, and Tools
questions.question: Two tools can automate browser tests. One integrates with the team's stack and is easy to maintain; the other has more marketing buzz but weaker fit. Which should the team prefer?
options: The better-fitting, maintainable tool that supports the team's workflow
The noisier tool because popularity predicts long-term success
The more expensive tool because cost implies quality
Whichever tool has the most features, regardless of learning curve
questions.explanation: Tool choice should be driven by suitability and maintainability in the team's context. Popularity alone does not ensure effectiveness.

questions.question: What is meant by a product increment at the end of a sprint?
options: A draft document describing what developers hope to build next
A potentially releasable piece of working product that meets the team's completion criteria
Any code committed to a private branch
A list of remaining defects for the release
questions.explanation: A sprint increment is working product, not just partial activity. It should satisfy the team's agreed completion standards.

questions.question: Which completion rule best supports quality within a sprint?
options: A story is done when coding ends, even if regression failures remain
A story is done only when agreed tests pass and outstanding critical defects are resolved or consciously accepted
A story is done when the stand-up mentions it twice
A story is done as soon as the product owner writes acceptance criteria
questions.explanation: Completion should reflect tested, usable work rather than coding alone. Passing agreed checks is part of meaningful done.

questions.question: Which behavior is LEAST aligned with the agile tester role?
options: Helping the team understand risks early
Acting as the lone gatekeeper who privately decides whether others may release
Collaborating on quality criteria during refinement
Sharing learning from exploratory sessions with developers
questions.explanation: Agile quality is a shared responsibility. A lone gatekeeper model creates bottlenecks and weakens whole-team ownership.

questions.chapter: 4. Agile Testing Methods, Techniques, and Tools
questions.question: A major UI redesign broke many end-to-end tests even though core behavior stayed the same. What improvement would MOST likely reduce future maintenance pain?
options: Add more pixel-based assertions to every screen
Move suitable checks to lower levels and keep UI tests focused on critical user journeys
Stop automating regressions entirely
Freeze the user interface so tests never change
questions.explanation: When too many checks depend on UI detail, maintenance cost rises. Pushing appropriate coverage lower and keeping UI tests selective creates a healthier suite.

questions.question: Which behavior best reflects a self-managing agile team?
options: Waiting for the project manager to assign every task in detail
Collaboratively deciding how to accomplish the sprint goal and who takes which work
Avoiding cross-skilling so specialization stays pure
Escalating every small technical decision to senior management
questions.explanation: Self-managing teams organize their own work to meet shared goals. They do not depend on detailed task assignment from outside the team.

questions.question: When should important non-functional testing be considered for a new feature?
options: Only in a separate hardening sprint after all features are complete
During story discussion and implementation so relevant quality risks are addressed within the iteration
Only after users report problems in production
After the release date is fixed and cannot change
questions.explanation: Important non-functional concerns should be surfaced early. Treating them late increases cost and risk.

questions.question: How does using concrete examples improve collaboration between testers, developers, and business representatives?
options: It removes the need for any conversation about requirements
It creates a shared reference for expected behavior that different roles can discuss clearly
It guarantees automation will be easy
It is only helpful after coding is complete
questions.explanation: Concrete examples make abstract requirements easier to discuss and verify. They help different roles align on the same intent.

questions.chapter: 4. Agile Testing Methods, Techniques, and Tools
questions.question: What best describes pair testing?
options: A tester and another teammate explore, discuss, and evaluate the product together in real time
Two testers independently execute the same script without speaking
A mandatory replacement for all automated testing
A way to split one defect report into two tickets
questions.explanation: Pair testing combines different perspectives during hands-on investigation. It often improves learning and shortens feedback cycles.

questions.question: What is the main benefit of an information radiator such as a visible task board?
options: It stores confidential management notes away from the team
It gives the team and stakeholders quick shared visibility into current work and progress
It replaces all direct communication
It measures source code complexity automatically
questions.explanation: Information radiators make important status information easy to see. That visibility supports alignment and timely conversations.

questions.question: Which defect report is MOST useful on an agile team?
options: A concise report with clear reproduction steps, observed result, and expected result
A one-line message saying 'broken' with no context
A 20-page template that omits screenshots and logs
A note stored privately until the sprint review
questions.explanation: Agile defect communication should be quick and actionable. Clear reproduction information helps the team respond efficiently.

questions.question: Customer support reports that 'checkout sometimes freezes' but provides little detail. What should the tester do first?
options: Close the issue until a full root-cause analysis is attached
Work with support and technical teammates to gather context that makes the problem reproducible or classifiable
Assume it is a user training problem
Rewrite the report as a passing acceptance criterion
questions.explanation: Vague field reports need clarification before the team can act effectively. Testers can help turn anecdotal symptoms into actionable information.

questions.chapter: 4. Agile Testing Methods, Techniques, and Tools
questions.question: Why can a specification workshop be more effective than emailing requirements back and forth?
options: It creates fast shared understanding and lets questions be resolved while examples are still being shaped
It guarantees zero future requirement changes
It removes the need for any written examples
It is useful only when no testers are on the team
questions.explanation: Interactive workshops surface misunderstandings quickly. They are especially effective when the team uses concrete examples to discuss behavior.

questions.question: A sprint burndown chart rises for two consecutive days. What is the BEST interpretation?
options: The team discovered or added more remaining work than it completed
The sprint is automatically considered failed
The team should stop testing to reduce the line
Burndown charts are only updated at sprint end
questions.explanation: An upward movement means the estimate of remaining work increased. That can happen when hidden work is uncovered or scope changes.

questions.question: Why do agile teams often prefer many lower-level automated tests and fewer end-to-end tests?
options: Because end-to-end tests are forbidden by agile methods
Because lower-level tests usually run faster and fail more precisely, supporting quick feedback
Because lower-level tests cover usability better
Because business stakeholders cannot understand end-to-end behavior
questions.explanation: Fast, focused lower-level checks provide efficient feedback and easier diagnosis. End-to-end tests remain useful, but usually in smaller numbers.

questions.question: Why do agile testers often prefer a quick conversation plus lightweight evidence over a long formal defect document?
options: Because speed and shared understanding are improved when information is timely and focused
Because agile teams never record defects
Because developers are not allowed to read written reports
Because quality data is unimportant in agile
questions.explanation: Agile communication aims to be efficient and useful. Lightweight evidence paired with conversation often resolves issues faster than heavy paperwork.

questions.chapter: 4. Agile Testing Methods, Techniques, and Tools
questions.question: How can feature flags support agile testing and release practices?
options: By allowing new behavior to be enabled selectively, reducing the risk of exposing all users at once
By eliminating the need for regression testing of flagged code
By replacing backlog prioritization
By ensuring unfinished features are automatically production-ready
questions.explanation: Feature flags can separate deployment from exposure. That gives teams more control over rollout and learning.

questions.question: Why do frequent releases reduce product risk?
options: Because releasing often guarantees zero production incidents
Because smaller changes reach users sooner and are easier to evaluate and roll back if needed
Because frequent releases remove the need for prioritization
Because they allow teams to skip regression testing
questions.explanation: Smaller, more frequent releases limit the size of each change set. That makes problems easier to detect, understand, and recover from.

questions.question: An intermittent defect appears only when a background job overlaps with checkout processing. What is the BEST agile testing response?
options: Close the issue until it can be reproduced by end users
Pair across roles to reproduce the timing conditions and learn enough to design targeted checks
Add more UI smoke tests and hope one eventually fails
Avoid investigating because intermittent defects are outside sprint scope
questions.explanation: Intermittent problems often require collaborative investigation. Reproducing the conditions helps the team create focused tests and fixes.

questions.question: A story was estimated without considering test environment setup and specialized data needs. How should a tester respond?
options: Say nothing so the team's estimate is not challenged
Raise the hidden work and risks so the team can make a more realistic commitment
Remove testing tasks from the sprint plan
Assume the product owner will discover the problem later
questions.explanation: A tester adds value by surfacing hidden quality work before commitments are locked in. Realistic planning depends on that visibility.

questions.chapter: 4. Agile Testing Methods, Techniques, and Tools
questions.question: Why are executable specifications valuable beyond the sprint in which they were created?
options: They serve as a maintainable behavioral reference when kept aligned with the product
They should be discarded once the initial feature is accepted
They are useful only to automation engineers
They make exploratory testing unnecessary forever
questions.explanation: Executable specifications can remain useful as long as they continue to reflect current behavior. They provide both documentation and repeatable verification.

questions.question: Why is technical excellence closely linked to business agility?
options: Because only architects benefit from clean code and reliable tests
Because strong engineering practices make change safer, faster, and less costly for the product
Because business agility depends mainly on writing more documentation
Because technical excellence matters only after the first release
questions.explanation: Reliable design, automation, and maintainable code reduce the friction of change. That helps the business respond quickly without sacrificing quality.

questions.chapter: 4. Agile Testing Methods, Techniques, and Tools
questions.question: What is the main benefit of adding automated security checks early in the pipeline where appropriate?
options: They can reveal certain classes of security issues earlier, when fixes are usually cheaper
They guarantee the product is fully secure for every threat
They remove the need for secure design discussions
They should replace all other non-functional testing
questions.explanation: Early automated security checks support faster feedback on some vulnerabilities or misconfigurations. They complement broader security practices.
